bss.topic: Relevo brasileiro: planaltos, planícies e depressões

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é relevo?
options: O conjunto de formas da superfície terrestre
O conjunto de rios de uma região
O tipo de clima de um lugar
questions.answer: O conjunto de formas da superfície terrestre
questions.hint: Pense em montanhas, vales e áreas planas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual forma de relevo é uma área elevada, com topo relativamente plano, onde predomina o desgaste (erosão)?
questions.hint: O nome lembra algo 'plano' e 'alto'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual forma de relevo é uma área plana e baixa onde predomina a deposição de sedimentos?
questions.hint: Os rios deixam ali areia e argila trazidas de outros lugares.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama a forma de relevo que fica mais baixa do que as áreas ao seu redor?
questions.hint: É como um 'afundamento' em relação ao entorno.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a diferença entre depressão relativa e depressão absoluta?
options: A relativa fica acima do nível do mar; a absoluta, abaixo
A relativa fica abaixo do nível do mar; a absoluta, acima
A relativa é sempre alagada; a absoluta, seca
questions.answer: A relativa fica acima do nível do mar; a absoluta, abaixo
questions.hint: Compare cada uma com o nível do mar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: As depressões do Brasil são de que tipo?
questions.hint: Nenhuma área do território brasileiro fica abaixo do nível do mar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual forma de relevo predomina no território brasileiro?
questions.hint: Pense na maior parte do interior do país.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o ponto mais alto do Brasil?
questions.hint: Fica no estado do Amazonas, perto da fronteira com a Venezuela.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o Brasil não tem cordilheiras altas como os Andes?
options: Seu relevo é formado por estruturas antigas e muito desgastadas pela erosão
Porque o Brasil fica no Hemisfério Norte
Porque não há rios no interior
questions.answer: Seu relevo é formado por estruturas antigas e muito desgastadas pela erosão
questions.hint: Pense na idade das rochas e no tempo de ação da chuva e do vento.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas é uma grande planície brasileira, alagada boa parte do ano?
questions.hint: Fica em Mato Grosso e Mato Grosso do Sul.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em um mapa de relevo, para que serve a legenda de cores?
options: Para indicar as faixas de altitude
Para mostrar os estados do país
questions.answer: Para indicar as faixas de altitude
questions.hint: Cada cor corresponde a um intervalo de metros.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em muitos mapas de relevo, as áreas mais baixas aparecem em verde. Que cores costumam indicar as áreas mais altas?
options: Branco e cinza-claro, só no litoral
questions.hint: As cores vão 'esquentando' conforme a altitude sobe.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quais agentes externos ajudam a modelar o relevo ao longo do tempo?
questions.hint: São forças que desgastam e transportam material na superfície.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A Serra do Mar, perto do litoral do Sudeste, é a borda de qual forma de relevo?
questions.hint: Quem sobe a serra chega a uma área elevada no interior.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que nas planícies predomina a sedimentação e nos planaltos predomina a erosão.
questions.hint: Pense para onde a água da chuva e os rios levam a terra.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Observe um mapa de relevo imaginário: uma área verde ao lado de um rio e uma área marrom no interior. Qual delas provavelmente é planície e qual é planalto? Justifique.
questions.hint: Relacione as cores da legenda com a altitude.

en.topic: Informative writing: leaflets and fact sheets

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main purpose of a leaflet or fact sheet?
questions.hint: Think about what the reader should learn.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a heading?
options: A title that tells the reader what a section is about
The last sentence of a paragraph
questions.answer: A title that tells the reader what a section is about
questions.hint: It usually sits at the top of a section.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does a subheading do?
options: Divides a section into smaller topics
questions.answer: Divides a section into smaller topics
questions.hint: It sits below a main heading.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is a fact?
options: Bees are the most beautiful insects.
Bee stings are the worst thing ever.
questions.hint: A fact can be checked and proved.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is an opinion?
options: The museum is the best day out in town.
Tickets for children cost less than adult tickets.
questions.answer: The museum is the best day out in town.
questions.hint: Look for a word that shows a personal view.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which feature helps readers find information quickly in a leaflet?
questions.hint: Think about what makes text easy to scan.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which tone suits a fact sheet about road safety for children?
questions.hint: The reader must understand and trust it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best heading for a section about what pandas eat?
questions.hint: It should tell the reader exactly what the section covers.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which connective is most useful for explaining a cause in informative writing?
questions.hint: Which word links a result to its reason?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which person is usually used in a fact sheet?
questions.hint: Think of 'it', 'they' and 'the planet'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which tense is mostly used to give general facts?
questions.hint: 'Sharks have no bones' is written in which tense?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What word describes subject-specific words such as 'habitat' or 'predator' in a fact sheet?
questions.hint: These words belong to a particular topic.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a glossary in a fact sheet?
options: A list of difficult words with their meanings
A list of the author's opinions
questions.answer: A list of difficult words with their meanings
questions.hint: It helps readers understand technical terms.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why might a leaflet include a 'Did you know?' box?
options: To tell a joke with no facts
questions.hint: Boxes draw the reader's eye.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write a short introduction (2–3 sentences) for a leaflet informing visitors about a local park.
questions.hint: Say what the park is and what the leaflet will explain.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain how headings and subheadings make a leaflet easier to read.
questions.hint: Think about how a reader finds the part they need.

en_read.topic: A Midsummer Night's Dream: plot and characters

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Where is A Midsummer Night's Dream mainly set?
questions.hint: The lovers run away from the city.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Who is the Duke of Athens in A Midsummer Night's Dream?
questions.hint: He is about to marry Hippolyta.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Whom is Theseus about to marry at the start of the play?
questions.hint: She is the Queen of the Amazons.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which young man does Hermia love?
questions.hint: Her father wants her to marry someone else.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Whom does Egeus want his daughter Hermia to marry?
questions.hint: It is not the man she loves.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: At the start of the play, whom does Helena love?
questions.hint: He used to love her but now wants Hermia.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Who are the king and queen of the fairies?
questions.hint: They argue in the wood.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What do Oberon and Titania quarrel about?
questions.hint: Each wants to keep a young child.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the name of Oberon's mischievous servant?
questions.hint: He is also called Robin Goodfellow.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does the juice of the magic flower do when put on sleeping eyes?
options: Makes the person fall in love with the first creature they see
Turns the person into a donkey
Makes the person forget their name
questions.answer: Makes the person fall in love with the first creature they see
questions.hint: It causes most of the confusion among the lovers.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What mistake does Puck make with the flower juice?
options: He puts it on Lysander instead of Demetrius
questions.answer: He puts it on Lysander instead of Demetrius
questions.hint: Both young men wear Athenian clothes.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which character's head is changed into a donkey's (ass's) head?
questions.hint: He is a weaver and one of the mechanicals.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Who are the 'mechanicals'?
options: Workmen who rehearse a play for the Duke's wedding
questions.answer: Workmen who rehearse a play for the Duke's wedding
questions.hint: They include a weaver, a carpenter and a joiner.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What play do the mechanicals perform?
questions.hint: It is a tragic love story they perform comically.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Describe Puck's character, using one thing he does in the play as evidence.
questions.hint: Is he careful or playful? What happens because of him?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do you think Helena feels unhappy for much of the play?
questions.hint: Think about who she loves and how he treats her.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: How is birth rate usually measured?
options: Live births per 1,000 people per year
Total births in a country ever
questions.answer: Live births per 1,000 people per year
questions.hint: Geographers compare countries using the same group size.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: How is death rate usually measured?
questions.hint: It is measured in the same way as birth rate.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is the term for the birth rate minus the death rate?
questions.hint: It ignores migration.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A country has a birth rate of 30 per 1,000 and a death rate of 10 per 1,000. What is the natural increase per 1,000 people?
questions.hint: Subtract the death rate from the birth rate.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A country has a birth rate of 12 per 1,000 and a death rate of 14 per 1,000. What is the natural change per 1,000 people? Use a minus sign if it is a decrease.
questions.hint: Which is bigger: births or deaths?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: If the death rate is higher than the birth rate and there is no migration, the population will:
questions.hint: More people are dying than being born.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Roughly what was the world population in 2022?
questions.hint: It passed a new billion milestone that year.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: When did world population begin to grow very rapidly?
options: From around 1800, with industrialisation and better medicine
questions.answer: From around 1800, with industrialisation and better medicine
questions.hint: Think about when farming, industry and health care changed quickly.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which factor most helps to reduce the death rate?
options: Clean water and better health care
questions.answer: Clean water and better health care
questions.hint: What stops people catching diseases?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which factor tends to reduce the birth rate?
options: More girls staying in education and access to family planning
questions.answer: More girls staying in education and access to family planning
questions.hint: Think about choices families make when they have more options.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What word describes people moving from one place to another, which also changes population?
questions.hint: It can be in or out of a country.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which shape best describes the graph of world population over the last 200 years?
questions.hint: Slow growth for a long time, then a steep rise.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why do birth rates often stay high in poorer farming communities?

Children are not allowed to work
questions.answer: Children help work on the land and support parents later
questions.hint: Think about what children may contribute to a family.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A town of 50,000 people has 600 births in one year. What is the birth rate per 1,000 people?
questions.hint: Find how many groups of 1,000 people there are.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: If the birth rate falls but the death rate stays the same, natural increase will:
questions.hint: Natural increase is the gap between the two rates.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain one reason why death rates fell in many countries during the 20th century.
questions.hint: Think about vaccines, medicine, food or clean water.
